name: hof
description: Higher-Order Function combinators.  Every combinator is generic: `T` is the value's type and `U` the result's, so the same `apply`, `map` or `fold` works over integers, floats, strings and structs. They were fixed to `fn(i64 -- i64)` until generic function-pointer parameters started unifying. Combinators are functions that combine or apply other functions in useful patterns. They enable functional programming without explicit temporary variables.  Three of them are `stack fn` and the rest bind their parameters, which is not an accident of who wrote what. A combinator that passes one value through one function -- `apply`, `when`, `unless` -- says what it means with no names at all: `apply` is the single word `call`, and `when` is "test it, then call it or throw it away". A combinator that uses a value twice or takes two functions does not: `bi` stack-direct is `pick rot call rot rot call`, which is correct, passes its tests, and tells the reader nothing. Both forms were written and run before choosing (see R47 in TODO.md). doccheck: page-context doccheck: page-setup [1 2 3] -> arr

functions.name: all
functions.description: Check if all elements satisfy a predicate.

returns.name: result
returns.description: 1 if all elements satisfy pred, 0 otherwise

examples: arr fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 0 > } hof::all  // all positive?

functions.name: any
functions.description: Check if any element satisfies a predicate.

returns.name: result
returns.description: 1 if any element satisfies pred, 0 otherwise

examples: arr fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 0 > } hof::any  // any positive?

functions.name: apply
functions.description: Apply a function to a value.
examples: 5 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::apply print nl  // 10

functions.name: bi_star
functions.signature: (x:T y:T f:fn(T -- U) g:fn(T -- U) -- a:U b:U)
functions.description: Apply two functions to two values (first to first, second to second).
examples: 3 4 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 1 + } fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::bi_star  // Stack: 4 8

functions.name: bi
functions.signature: (x:T f:fn(T -- U) g:fn(T -- U) -- a:U b:U)
functions.description: Apply two functions to the same value.

functions.name: both
functions.description: Apply a function to two values separately.
examples: 3 4 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x dup * } hof::both  // Stack: 9 16

functions.name: dip
functions.description: Apply a function to the second stack element, preserving the top.

functions.name: filter
functions.description: Filter an array, keeping only elements that satisfy a predicate.
examples: arr fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 mod 0 == } hof::filter  // keep evens

functions.name: find
functions.description: Find the first element satisfying a predicate.

returns.name: elem
returns.description: The found element (or 0 if not found)

examples: arr fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 10 > } hof::find  // first > 10

functions.name: fold
functions.description: Fold/reduce an array left-to-right with a binary function.
examples: arr 0 fn (acc:i64 x:i64 -- r:i64) { acc x + } hof::fold  // sum of array

functions.name: fold_right
functions.description: Fold/reduce an array right-to-left with a binary function.
examples: arr 0 fn (x:i64 acc:i64 -- r:i64) { x acc + } hof::fold_right  // sum of array

functions.name: keep
functions.description: Apply a function but keep the original value.

functions.name: map
functions.description: Map a function over an array, returning a new array.
examples: arr fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::map  // double each element

functions.name: times
functions.description: Apply function n times to an initial value.
examples: 2 4 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x dup * } hof::times print nl  // 65536 (2^16)

functions.name: tri
functions.signature: (x:T f:fn(T -- U) g:fn(T -- U) h:fn(T -- U) -- a:U b:U c:U)
functions.description: Apply three functions to the same value.
examples: 5 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 1 + } fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x dup * } hof::tri  // Stack: 6 10 25

functions.name: unless
functions.description: Apply function only if condition is false, otherwise return value unchanged.

returns.name: r
returns.description: Result of f(x) if cond is false, otherwise x

examples: 5 0 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::unless print nl  // 10
5 1 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::unless print nl  // 5

functions.name: when
functions.description: Apply function only if condition is true, otherwise return value unchanged.

returns.name: r
returns.description: Result of f(x) if cond is true, otherwise x

examples: 5 1 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::when print nl  // 10
5 0 fn (x:i64 -- r:i64) { x 2 * } hof::when print nl  // 5
